title: Marie Curie
text: Marie Curie was a Polish and naturalized-French physicist and chemist who conducted pioneering research on radioactivity.

title: Marie Curie
text: Marie Curie was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, the first person to win two Nobel Prizes, and the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different scientific fields.

title: Marie Curie
text: Curie was awarded the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics alongside Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel.

title: Marie Curie
text: Curie won the 1911 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for her discovery of the elements radium and polonium.

title: Marie Curie
text: Marie Curie died in 1934 from aplastic anemia caused by prolonged exposure to ionizing radiation during her scientific research.

title: Albert Einstein
text: Albert Einstein was a German-born theoretical physicist widely held to be one of the greatest and most influential scientists of all time.

title: Albert Einstein
text: Einstein is best known for developing the theory of relativity, but he also made important contributions to quantum mechanics.

title: Albert Einstein
text: Einstein received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for his services to theoretical physics, and especially for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect.

title: Albert Einstein
text: Einstein did not receive a Nobel Prize for his theory of general relativity due to skepticism from the Nobel committee at the time.

title: Albert Einstein
text: In 1933, Einstein emigrated to the United States to escape Nazi persecution and became a professor at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton.

title: Apollo 11
text: Apollo 11 was the American spaceflight that first landed humans on the Moon on July 20, 1969.

title: Neil Armstrong
text: Neil Armstrong was an American astronaut and aeronautical engineer who became the first person to walk on the Moon.

title: Buzz Aldrin
text: Buzz Aldrin was the lunar module pilot on Apollo 11 and the second person to walk on the Moon.

title: Michael Collins
text: Michael Collins was the command module pilot of Apollo 11 and remained in lunar orbit while Armstrong and Aldrin walked on the Moon.

title: Mars
text: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and the second-smallest planet in the Solar System, larger only than Mercury.

title: Mars Exploration
text: NASA's Perseverance rover landed on Mars inside Jezero crater on February 18, 2021.

title: Jupiter
text: Jupiter is the fifth planet from the Sun and the largest in the Solar System, being more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined.

title: Australia
text: Canberra is the capital city of Australia, founded following the compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne in 1908.

title: Sydney
text: Sydney is the most populous city in Australia and the state capital of New South Wales, but it is not the national capital.

title: Canada
text: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada, located in the province of Ontario on the southern bank of the Ottawa River.

title: Toronto
text: Toronto is the capital of Ontario and the most populous city in Canada, but not the federal capital.

title: Japan
text: Tokyo is the capital and most populous prefecture of Japan, located at the head of Tokyo Bay.

title: Mount Everest
text: Mount Everest is Earth's highest mountain above sea level, located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas, on the China-Nepal border.

title: Nile River
text: The Nile is generally considered the longest river in the world, flowing through northeastern Africa into the Mediterranean Sea.

title: Amazon River
text: The Amazon River in South America is the largest river by discharge volume of water in the world and the second longest.

title: World War II
text: World War II was a global war that lasted from 1939 to 1945, involving the vast majority of the world's countries forming the Allies and the Axis.

title: World War II
text: World War II began in Europe on September 1, 1939, when Nazi Germany invaded Poland, leading the UK and France to declare war.

title: United Nations
text: The United Nations is an intergovernmental organization founded in 1945 following World War II to prevent future world wars.

title: United Nations
text: The UN Charter was signed on June 26, 1945, in San Francisco, and came into force on October 24, 1945.

title: League of Nations
text: The League of Nations was the predecessor to the United Nations, established in 1920 after the Paris Peace Conference.

title: DNA
text: Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) is a polymer composed of two polynucleotide chains that coil around each other to form a double helix.

title: DNA Structure
text: The molecular structure of DNA was first identified by James Watson and Francis Crick in 1953 with data from Rosalind Franklin.

title: Penicillin
text: Penicillin was discovered in 1928 by Scottish physician and microbiologist Alexander Fleming at St. Mary's Hospital in London.

title: Penicillin
text: Penicillin is an antibiotic derived from Penicillium fungi used to treat bacterial infections, not viral infections.

title: Vaccines
text: Edward Jenner is widely considered the pioneer of the smallpox vaccine, the world's first successful vaccine developed in 1796.

title: Human Heart
text: The human heart has four chambers: two upper atria (receiving chambers) and two lower ventricles (pumping chambers).

title: Alan Turing
text: Alan Turing was an English mathematician, computer scientist, logician, and cryptanalyst who played a pivotal role in cracking intercepted coded messages during World War II at Bletchley Park.

title: Alan Turing
text: Turing is widely considered to be the father of theoretical computer science and artificial intelligence.

title: World Wide Web
text: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at CERN in Geneva, Switzerland.

title: Python Programming Language
text: Python is a high-level, general-purpose programming language conceived in the late 1980s by Guido van Rossum at CWI in the Netherlands.

title: Linux
text: Linux is an open-source Unix-like operating system kernel created by Linus Torvalds and released on September 17, 1991.

title: Transistor
text: The point-contact transistor was invented in December 1947 by John Bardeen, Walter Brattain, and William Shockley at Bell Labs.

title: William Shakespeare
text: William Shakespeare was an English playwright, poet, and actor, widely regarded as the greatest writer in the English language.

title: William Shakespeare
text: Shakespeare's works include 39 plays, 154 sonnets, and three long narrative poems, including Hamlet, Romeo and Juliet, and Macbeth.

title: Leonardo da Vinci
text: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper, and was a leading figure of the Italian High Renaissance.

title: Mona Lisa
text: The Mona Lisa is a portrait painted in oil on a poplar panel, currently housed in the Louvre Museum in Paris.

title: Vincent van Gogh
text: Vincent van Gogh was a Dutch Post-Impressionist painter who created about 2,100 artworks, including The Starry Night painted in June 1889.

title: European Union
text: The European Union is a political and economic union of 27 member states located primarily in Europe.

title: Brexit
text: The United Kingdom formally left the European Union on January 31, 2020, following a public referendum held in June 2016.

title: Federal Reserve
text: The Federal Reserve System is the central banking system of the United States, created on December 23, 1913, with the Federal Reserve Act.

title: Barack Obama
text: Barack Obama served as the 44th president of the United States from 2009 to 2017, and was the first African-American president in US history.

title: Nelson Mandela
text: Nelson Mandela was a South African anti-apartheid activist and politician who served as the first president of South Africa from 1994 to 1999.

title: Nobel Peace Prize
text: Nelson Mandela and F. W. de Klerk jointly received the 1993 Nobel Peace Prize for their work in peacefully ending the apartheid regime.

title: Max Planck
text: Max Planck was awarded the 1918 Nobel Prize in Physics in recognition of the services he rendered to the advancement of Physics by his discovery of energy quanta.

title: Niels Bohr
text: Niels Bohr received the 1922 Nobel Prize in Physics for his services in the investigation of the structure of atoms and of the radiation emanating from them.

title: Wilhelm Röntgen
text: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen was awarded the inaugural Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901 for the discovery of X-rays.

title: Pierre Curie
text: Pierre Curie was a French physicist and pioneer in crystallography, magnetism, and radioactivity who shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics.

title: Ernest Rutherford
text: Ernest Rutherford was awarded the 1908 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for his investigations into the disintegration of the elements and the chemistry of radioactive substances.

title: Apollo 12
text: Apollo 12 was the sixth crewed flight in the Apollo program and the second to land on the Moon, carrying astronauts Charles Pete Conrad and Alan Bean in November 1969.

title: Apollo 13
text: Apollo 13 was intended to be the third lunar landing, but an oxygen tank exploded two days after launch, forcing the crew to abort the landing and return to Earth.

title: Apollo 17
text: Apollo 17 was the final mission of NASA's Apollo program, during which Eugene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt spent over three days on the lunar surface in December 1972.

title: Space Shuttle Columbia
text: Space Shuttle Columbia was the first space-rated orbiter in NASA's Space Shuttle fleet, first launched on April 12, 1981.

title: International Space Station
text: The International Space Station is the largest modular space station in low Earth orbit, involving five participating space agencies including NASA, Roscosmos, and ESA.

title: Melbourne
text: Melbourne served as the interim seat of government of Australia from federation in 1901 until 1927 when the new capital of Canberra was inaugurated.

title: Brisbane
text: Brisbane is the capital and most populous city of the Australian state of Queensland, and the third most populous city in Australia.

title: Perth
text: Perth is the capital and largest city of Western Australia, located along the Swan River on Australia's southwestern coast.

title: Adelaide
text: Adelaide is the capital city of South Australia, founded in 1836 as the planned capital for a freely-settled British province.

title: Howard Florey
text: Australian pathologist Howard Florey shared the 1945 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Alexander Fleming and Ernst Boris Chain for extracting and clinical purifying penicillin.

title: Louis Pasteur
text: Louis Pasteur was a French chemist and microbiologist renowned for discovering the principles of vaccination, microbial fermentation, and pasteurization.

title: Rabies Vaccine
text: The first successful vaccine against rabies was developed in 1885 by Louis Pasteur and Émile Roux using an attenuated virus.

title: Robert Koch
text: Robert Koch was a German physician who identified the specific causative agents of tuberculosis, cholera, and anthrax, winning the 1905 Nobel Prize.

title: Antibiotics vs Antivirals
text: Antibiotics are antimicrobial medications used in the treatment and prevention of bacterial infections; they are completely ineffective against viruses such as the common cold or influenza.

title: Robert Cailliau
text: Belgian informatics engineer Robert Cailliau collaborated with Tim Berners-Lee on the World Wide Web project and co-authored the first formal funding proposal for it at CERN in 1990.

title: ARPANET
text: The Advanced Research Projects Agency Network (ARPANET) was the first wide-area packet-switched network with distributed control, establishing its first permanent link in October 1969.

title: Vinton Cerf
text: Vinton Cerf and Bob Kahn designed the TCP/IP protocols and the architecture of the Internet, receiving the Turing Award in 2004.

title: Marc Andreessen
text: Marc Andreessen co-authored Mosaic, the first widely used graphical Web browser, released by NCSA at the University of Illinois in 1993.

title: Treaty of Rome
text: The Treaty of Rome was signed on March 25, 1957, establishing the European Economic Community (EEC) among France, West Germany, Italy, and the Benelux nations.

title: Maastricht Treaty
text: The Maastricht Treaty, signed in February 1992, founded the European Union and laid the groundwork for the creation of the single European currency, the Euro.

title: United Kingdom EEC Entry
text: The United Kingdom acceded to the European Communities (the predecessor to the EU) on January 1, 1973, alongside Denmark and Ireland.

title: 2016 Brexit Referendum
text: On June 23, 2016, the United Kingdom held an advisory referendum in which 51.9 percent of participating voters voted in favor of leaving the European Union.

title: San Francisco Conference
text: The United Nations Conference on International Organization took place in San Francisco from April 25 to June 26, 1945, resulting in the creation of the United Nations Charter.

title: UN Security Council
text: The United Nations Security Council is one of the six principal organs of the UN, charged with ensuring international peace and security with five permanent veto-wielding members.

title: American Civil War
text: The American Civil War was fought between the United States of America and the Confederate States from 1861 to 1865, resulting in the preservation of the Union and the abolition of slavery.

title: Michelangelo
text: Michelangelo Buonarroti was an Italian sculptor, painter, and architect of the High Renaissance who sculpted the marble statue of David and painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling.

title: Raphael
text: Raphael was an Italian painter and architect whose work is admired for its clarity of form and ease of composition, notably The School of Athens in the Vatican.

title: The Last Supper
text: The Last Supper is a late 15th-century mural painting by Leonardo da Vinci housed by the refectory of the Convent of Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan, Italy.

title: United States Constitution
text: The Constitution of the United States was framed and signed on September 17, 1787, by delegates at the Constitutional Convention in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

title: Declaration of Independence
text: The United States Declaration of Independence was adopted by the Second Continental Congress in Philadelphia on July 4, 1776, declaring the thirteen colonies free from British rule.

title: Panic of 1907
text: The Panic of 1907 was a United States financial crisis that took place over a three-week period starting in mid-October, leading directly to the creation of the Federal Reserve System.

title: Woodrow Wilson
text: Woodrow Wilson served as the 28th president of the United States from 1913 to 1921, signing into law the Federal Reserve Act and leading the nation through World War I.

title: F. W. de Klerk
text: Frederik Willem de Klerk was the state president of South Africa from 1989 to 1994, who oversaw the end of apartheid and the transition to multi-racial democracy alongside Nelson Mandela.
